detail: Story Decisions state count is validated before the item lookup (400 even for an unknown id). The plan lists this as an open question. Add a functional case: GET /api/catalog/items/999999/brand-mates?count=0 returns 400 problem details, not 404.
location: Implementation Notes / Decisions; plan Open questions

detail: Story states a failed brand-mates call (HTTP error, timeout, bad JSON) is logged and the page renders without the section. The plan marks it undefined and out of scope. Add an e2e case where the brand-mates request fails (for example a Playwright route intercept returning 500) and /item/1001 still shows the product details and no 'More from' heading. If that is not reachable, name the observable version.
location: Implementation Notes / Decisions; plan Out of scope

detail: AC6 says 'up to four' cards and the heading shows whenever the endpoint returns items. No case covers a brand with 1 to 3 other items, which should show the heading with exactly those cards. Seed such a brand and add an e2e or functional case.
Story states Id is the tie-breaker for identical names, but the plan calls tie order unspecified. Add a case with two same-name items, or accept the gap as minor.
Prices are 'as the catalog formats prices'. State the exact rendered strings or say to compare with the catalog list card.

The case requires each of the four cards to have a picture. In the keyframe every card shows a broken-image icon with alt text, because the scenario's <id>.webp files do not exist on the stack. The test only asserts img toBeVisible, which passes for a broken image.
The signed-in frame shows the same four cards with broken images. The case reuses the TC-11 card expectations, and the shared helper does not check that the image loaded.
The case requires India Rope and Juliet Cup each to have a picture. The frame shows broken images, and the test asserts only that the img element is visible.

The functional cases (01 to 10, 15, 17) specify Catalog.API in-process with CatalogApiFixture, but the tests are Playwright API calls against the full test stack, and the scenario is named cat-1 rather than brand-mates. The contract is still exercised against real Postgres, so this is minor.

The demo.absent frame is taken on the title heading and shows only the top of /item/1008 (Lone Compass, price, image cropped at the fold). The area below the details, where the 'More from' section would appear, is not in view, so the frame does not show the absence. The spec should scroll to or frame the region below the product details before demo.absent.

Functional cases 01-10, 15 and 17 specify Catalog.API in-process with CatalogApiFixture, but the tests are Playwright request calls against the full teststack. The real API and Postgres are still exercised and all assertions match, so the impact is minor.

Functional cases TC-CAT-1-01 to 10, 15 and 17 run as Playwright API calls against the deployed test stack instead of the in-process Catalog.API with CatalogApiFixture the cases name. The real Postgres and the HTTP contract are still exercised, so this is low severity. TC-05's non-array check is also weak: it wraps JSON.parse in a try/catch and would fail on an empty body.

The expected result says the unit price is '(.00 and .00)' and that each line has 'its picture'. State the exact prices (Cedar Headlamp $25.00, Alpine Pack $40.00) and the observable picture check (an img with the product's name as alt text and a non-empty src). Also say whether the saved-list order (Cedar Headlamp, then Alpine Pack) is asserted, since the story does not define it. Prefer asserting the set of saved lines, not their order.

TC-15 and TC-13 both store a basket with Items and SavedItems via UpdateBasketAsync and read it back from real Redis, checking the same fields. Merge them into one case, for example a single round-trip with two saved products read by a second repository instance, and drop the AC1/AC8 'covers' claim, which a plain repository round-trip does not prove.

The story says deleting the basket 'empties the cart'. It does not say the Redis key is removed or that GetBasketAsync then returns null. That detail comes from Implementation Notes. Assert only that the cart is empty (null or an empty basket) and that nothing saved remains, or mark the null result as an implementation decision.

The case asserts the header cart link has no .cart-button-count element when the cart is empty. The story only says saved products are excluded from the badge count and does not say the badge is hidden at zero. Assert that the badge shows no count, or a count of 0, as the existing CartMenu behavior defines, and cite that behavior.

Step 1 says 'complete the checkout form as it is prefilled and press the place-order button', and the case relies on unstated default-scenario profile data. Name the exact controls (button labels or selectors), the expected redirect after placing the order, and how the new order is identified on /user/orders. Say how the test waits for the asynchronous order-started event that deletes the basket before step 3.

AC9 NOT_FOUND cases (TC-CART-1-07/08/09) only use an existing basket. Add a unit case, or extend those cases, where GetBasketAsync returns null (new shopper with no basket) for SaveForLater, MoveToCart and RemoveSavedItem. Expect RpcException NotFound and no UpdateBasketAsync call, rather than a NullReferenceException or an Internal error.

The absent keyframe highlights .cart-summary at the top of the page; the area below the cart where the Saved for later section would appear is off-screen, so the frame does not prove the section is absent.
The absent keyframe shows the empty-bag hero cut off at the viewport bottom; the place where the saved section would render is not visible.

The case requires the new order's total to be $90.00. The test asserts that any .order-total contains $90.00 and none contains $165.00, then highlights .first() without asserting that it is the new order. A pre-existing $90.00 order could satisfy the first check.
BASE_URL is handled inconsistently: signIn uses page.goto(BASE_URL ?? '/') while every other navigation uses `${BASE_URL}/...`. The spec loads scenario cart-1 while the plans name save-for-later.

The plan files for the e2e cases (TC-CART-1-16 to TC-CART-1-21) say `loadScenario('save-for-later')`, but the repository scenario is `.factory/stack/scenarios/cart-1` and the spec loads `cart-1`. Lesson L1 treats scenario names in plans that do not exist in the repository as a gap. The plan text should say `cart-1`.
The e2e plan cases (TC-CART-1-16 to 21) say loadScenario('save-for-later'), but the scenario in the repository and the spec is 'cart-1'. The plan names a scenario that does not exist.
The unit cases name tests/Basket.UnitTests/BasketServiceTests.cs, but the tests are in a new SaveForLaterTests.cs. The tests are faithful, so this only differs from the plan's location.

The title says 'an unknown brand id or an unknown type id' but the steps and expected result only exercise brand id 999 on v1. Either retitle it to brand only, or add a second PUT v1 step with an unknown type id and the expected 'Catalog type with id 999 does not exist.' detail.

Tests share one scenario load in serial mode. The count 101 assertions in TC-01 and TC-02 and the count 102 in TC-08 only hold because of execution order. TC-10 mutates item 1 for any later test. Order-dependent shared mutable state, and the 101-item list check is duplicated between TC-01 and TC-02.
The three event names are looped inside one [Fact], not run as [Theory] with [InlineData] rows. The case calls for a data-driven run, and a failure on the first name hides the rest.

e2e/teststack/bug-16.spec.ts re-implements the functional case through the full compose stack with a bearer token from the identity service, though the case specifies the functional layer with the test auth header. It is a redundant duplicate with brittle token-acquisition setup.

The case is layer 'functional' (in-process via WebhooksApiFixture, X-Test-User identity). The only test for it is e2e/teststack/bug-16.spec.ts, which runs against the compose test stack with a real identity-issued token for alice and a real webhooksclient receiver. No test in Bug16Tests.cs covers event '99', although AssertRejectedAndNothingStored('99') would implement it directly. If the e2e layer is intended, the case should be rewritten.
Three event names are looped inside one [Fact]; per lesson L1 they should be separate theory rows (InlineData) so each name's failure is isolated.
TC-02 has identical preconditions and steps to TC-01 (POST with no body); it only adds content-type and status-field assertions. Merge those assertions into TC-01 and drop TC-02.

TC-BUG-15-03, -04 and -05 repeat identical post-and-assert code differing only by the request body, in both OrderDraftValidationTests.cs and bug-15.spec.ts; a Theory with InlineData would avoid the duplication.

Outputs: 'below the cart lines and the order total, a section headed exactly Saved for later (N)'. TC-17 checks the position only for an empty cart; no case checks it when the cart has lines. TC-16 should assert that the 'Saved for later (2)' heading comes after the last cart line and the order total element, by DOM order or by bounding-box y position.

cart-1-saved.spec.ts copies signIn and the selector helpers (cartLines, cartLine, savedSection, savedLine, savedHeading, orderTotal, badge) from cart-1.spec.ts; signIn differs only in its user type union. They should be in a shared helper module imported by both specs.
